questions.question: What is CSS Grid?
questions.explanation: CSS Grid is a two-dimensional layout system for creating web page layouts.

questions.question: What is Flexbox?
questions.explanation: Flexbox is a one-dimensional layout method for arranging items in rows or columns.

questions.question: What is the box model in CSS?
questions.explanation: The CSS box model consists of content, padding, border, and margin areas.

questions.question: What is a CSS selector?
questions.explanation: A CSS selector is a pattern used to select and style HTML elements.

questions.question: What is the difference between class and ID selectors?
options: Class can be used multiple times, ID is unique
ID can be used multiple times, class is unique
Class is for styling, ID is for JavaScript
questions.explanation: Class selectors can be used on multiple elements, while ID selectors should be unique.

questions.question: What is a media query?
questions.explanation: Media queries are used for responsive design to apply styles based on screen size.

questions.question: What is the z-index property?
questions.explanation: Z-index controls the stacking order of positioned elements.

questions.question: What is a pseudo-class?
questions.explanation: A pseudo-class is a keyword that specifies a special state of an element.

questions.question: What is the difference between inline and block elements?
options: Inline flows horizontally, block starts new line
Block flows horizontally, inline starts new line
Inline is for text, block is for images
questions.explanation: Inline elements flow horizontally, while block elements start on a new line.

questions.question: What is CSS specificity?
questions.explanation: CSS specificity determines which styles are applied when there are conflicting rules.

questions.question: What is a CSS variable?
questions.explanation: CSS variables (custom properties) allow you to store and reuse values.

questions.question: What is the transform property?
questions.explanation: The transform property applies visual effects like rotate, scale, and translate.

questions.question: What is a CSS animation?
questions.explanation: CSS animations use keyframes to create complex animated effects.

questions.question: What is the difference between position relative and absolute?
options: Relative to normal flow, absolute to nearest positioned parent
Absolute to normal flow, relative to nearest positioned parent
Relative is for text, absolute is for images
questions.explanation: Relative positioning is relative to normal flow, absolute is relative to nearest positioned parent.

questions.question: What is a CSS framework?
questions.explanation: A CSS framework is a pre-built CSS system that provides ready-to-use styles and components.
